Nº 10
Axtor
Argentina, Glitch Artist
“This change in paradigm gives esteem to digital arts, something that didn’t happen. Once somebody told me: ‘digital is a quite unworthy format’. I’ll never forget that. Now the tables have turned and it is great, a new market is open in which the ‘unworthy’ has become the most noble thing on the planet.”

I feel like I’m swimming against the current. I always liked doing digital art. When I would do these types of works, I was told: ‘You have to paint, you have to do physical formats’. Now that I’m doing an analogical piece, the digital world is rising. Well, finally my time has come.

The analogical and the digital always went hand in hand. As a kid, I painted and suddenly got my hands on a computer and found that one could use Paint, and it was crazy for me. I did my drawings in Paint, then in Photoshop, then in Illustrator and when I discovered the vectorial format I went crazy as I thought: ‘this is endless’. In the year 2000, it was the Flash boom. I had my own webpage where I posted a lot of my digital works, short animations, interactive pieces where if you clicked something it would take you somewhere else. Years later I found out that it is called Webart.

I generated my own content. Filters didn’t exist at the time, so I would spend hours in Photoshop to process my image so that it would stand out. Today, being massive, the treatment of images has lost a little romance. You already have 700 filters on Instagram. I loved that era, but digital was not valued back then. I think it is important to give light to those times, and relive that stage.
